Header: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (ClearSight ML), Samir Khan (ClearSight Platform), Olivia Brooks (ClearSight PM)

Topics: benchmark results (latency & throughput) vs baseline provider; tuning (batching, kv cache, quant); dedicated vs hosted; security/sso/KMS; next steps

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, quick check - audio ok?
[00:06] Maya: yeah, loud and clear for me.
[00:08] Avery: cool. so last week we promised the side-by-side of the baseline provider runs vs Redwood bench. diego, do you want to walk the high level and then we can dig in?
[00:18] Diego: yeah, sure. i'll share my screen - (brief pause) - ok i got the spreadsheet up, link is in the chat: https://redwood.internal/bench/clearsight-2026-06 (note: internal link obfuscated).
[00:35] Diego: top line, we ran the same prompt set that maya sent - 12k requests, mixed short and medium prompts, seq len 64/128 median. baseline provider reported p95 of 212ms for their hosted endpoint, throughput ~430 reqs/min under the sample. our hosted runs show p95 ~145ms and throughput ~620 reqs/min with default batching and prefix cache enabled.
[01:02] Maya: that's a decent bump, did you run with the same concurrency pattern? baseline was running a bursty workload right?
[01:10] Diego: yep we matched the bursty pattern - we ran the 95th-percentile traffic window. two notes: baseline had KV cache disabled in their published run, we enabled prefix KV cache which is consistent with how you configured prod test earlier. when we disable prefix cache our p95 increases to around 190ms, so cache is contributing ~20-30% to latency reduction.
[01:34] Samir: ok curious about tail p99 - last time baseline had bad tail spikes which killed our SLA. how did p99 look?
[01:41] Diego: p99 is mixed - Redwood p99 is about 780ms in the hosted run, baseline p99 ~920ms. the variance is driven by bursts where batching builds up; we see improvements if we tune max_batch_ms down from 20ms to 10ms for latency-sensitive routes, but throughput drops ~8%.
[02:03] Olivia: that's the classic trade-off, we want stable tail for interactive features. is that tuning something we can do per-route?
[02:10] Avery: yes, per-route SLOs can be configured - you can set lower max_batch_ms for chat endpoints, keep higher for background generation. we'll document suggested profiles.
[02:19] Maya: can you speak to quantization - we saw some notes about int8 runs? accuracy regressions?
[02:24] Diego: we ran int8 quant for the medium latency profile; accuracy diff was within your eval tolerance - about 0.6% BLEU-like degradation on the token-level eval you provided. latency p95 dropped another 40-50ms and throughput improved ~12%. there's a small risk for some instruction-following prompts - we flagged a handful in the sample.
[02:47] Maya: ok flagged prompts are small set, we can share them.
[02:50] Diego: also did a dedicated-cluster run on the same hardware that baseline quoted (A100 80GB equiv) - on dedicated we saw throughput jump to 1100 reqs/min and p95 ~120ms, p99 ~450ms; baseline's dedicated numbers were 900 reqs/min, p95 ~150ms. so dedicated helps, but you do pay for reserved capacity.
[03:12] Samir: important: what's the deploy model for dedicated? we need VPC peering, strict egress rules.
[03:18] Avery: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed network; we can provision a private control plane and we support KMS/HSM for keys. diego will follow up with the exact peering checklist.
[03:29] Diego: i'll paste the peering doc after the call, it's also in the deck we shared.
[03:33] Olivia: curious about cost: you show throughput upside, but what's the cost delta vs baseline?
[03:39] Diego: rough numbers - hosted per-token unit costs are within 5% of baseline for typical sample when caching is active; dedicated reserved price yields 20-30% lower unit cost at scale, but requires commit. we'll put a price model in the spreadsheet.
[03:55] Maya: on the point of caching: does Redwood support prefix caching with invalidation? we need to ensure user-updated content isn't stale.
[04:02] Diego: yes, prefix/KV cache supports TTLs and manual invalidation APIs. you can scope cache to route or customer.
[04:09] Samir: security - SOC2, SSO, audit logs - what do you have for Private/Dedicated?
[04:15] Avery: we have SOC2 Type II, ISO docs available; dedicated + private deployments allow you to manage keys (KMS/HSM) and we emit audit logs for request-level tracing. i'll share the security pack after.
[04:25] Maya: perfect. one more question: did you test model fallbacks? if capacity spikes, does Redwood auto-fallback to smaller quantized model?
[04:33] Diego: yes we tested routing policy - during a simulated capacity constraint we routed 10% traffic to a quantized 7B variant; latency increased slightly for those requests but overall SLA remained intact. fallback is policy-driven and configurable.
[04:46] Olivia: nice. can we run an A/B to compare quality impact for our key flows?
[04:50] Avery: absolutely - that's a good next step: dedicated run with A/B on the flagged prompts. diego, can you prepare canary config?
[04:57] Diego: will do.
[05:00] Maya: on the test stack - one discrepancy i noticed in the sheet: baseline's measurement counted connection setup time differently; did you normalize for cold starts?
[05:09] Diego: good catch - we normalized to steady-state after warmup window to avoid cold-start skew. baseline's public report included cold-starts; when we add cold-starts to our numbers p95 moves to ~170ms. we documented both warm and warm+cold numbers in the CSV.
[05:26] Samir: scheduling: we need dedicated cluster run with our traffic sample - how long to spin up?
[05:31] Avery: for Redwood Dedicated we can provision a test cluster in 48-72 hours once peering and infra window are confirmed. Diego: technically we can do a short dev cluster in same-day for quick checks but full isolated test needs the peering window.
[05:44] Olivia: okay next steps sound straightforward. for the action items - can we get the raw CSV and the command lines so our infra team can reproduce?
[05:52] Diego: yep that's in my to-do - will share the full runbook.
[05:56] Maya: one last small thing - do you have token-level cost breakdown per-route?
[06:00] Diego: yes, Redwoods Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown per-route; we'll export a sample per your routes and include in the sheet.
[06:08] Avery: cool. any blockers from the Clearsight side?
[06:11] Maya: need to confirm security review timeline, but otherwise we can meet the dates.
[06:15] Samir: i'll confirm peering window by EOD tomorrow.
[06:18] Avery: perfect. quick recap - i'll send the benchmark CSV + security pack by Friday (2026-07-02), diego will prepare dedicated-run config and canary plan, maya will upload traffic sample, samir confirms peering window. we reconvene after dedicated run scheduling.
[06:33] Olivia: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[06:36] Avery: thanks all, talk soon.
